title: Per-request signal classifier for graceful degradation and circuit isolation
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We need a robust, low-latency mechanism to decide when an incoming request should be routed to a fallback model variant or isolated by a circuit breaker. Current routing reacts to coarse aggregated signals (per-region error rates and token-level throttles) which causes noisy global failovers and customer-visible flaps.

Goal: Implement a per-request signal classification layer that combines immediate signals (HTTP 429, per-request timeout, RPC error), short-window aggregations (10s/30s error rates for the tenant + region), and contextual heuristics (model variant compatibility, SLAs, tenant priority) to make deterministic fallback and isolation decisions. The classifier should support:
- Fast inference (<2ms) on the routing path.
- Configurable thresholds and hysteresis windows per tenant and per tier.
- Stateful probation + decay for tenants that triggered a circuit.
- Observability hooks and reasons for every automatic fallback.

Non‑goals: This ticket does not implement the UI controls in Console (separate PM ticket) or the long-term ML model for signal learning — initial classifier will be rule-based with a simple score function and feature weights.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routing path returns a structured fallback_reason string when a request is routed to a fallback variant or short-circuited.
2) Per-request decision latency <= 2ms p95 under baseline load.
3) Default tenant profile yields no false positives in the synthetic surge test (no more than 1% unnecessary fallbacks).
4) Telemetry emitted: decision_score, contributing_signals, tenant_policy_id, circuit_state.
5) Integration test that simulates 429 bursts/timeouts causes localized (tenant/region) isolations rather than global rollbacks.
technical_notes:
Design: add a lightweight classifier component in the router service (router-core) that computes a numeric trip_score. Score inputs: immediate_signal (enum: 429, timeout, rpc_err), short_window_error_rate (tenant+region for 10s/30s), recent_latency_spike_ratio, concurrent_inflight_ratio, variant_compatibility_penalty.

Policy semantics: trip_score >= tenant_threshold => tentatively mark request for fallback; successive affirmative decisions within probation_window escalate to OPEN circuit for the tenant+region+variant tuple. Circuit state machine: CLOSED -> PROBATION -> OPEN -> DECAYING -> CLOSED. Decay uses exponential backoff with configurable half-life.

Performance: classifier implemented in Rust (router-core) with a frozen small table of tenant thresholds for O(1) lookup. Fallback decision is deterministic and memoized per-request until response.

Data model: store circuit state and last_trip_timestamp in redis cluster with TTLs to support cross-router state. Use shard key (tenant_id:region:variant). Redis latency budget: <=1ms local cache + async refresh.

Trade-offs: Using Redis introduces cross-node statefulness; mitigated by strong local caching and short TTLs. Alternative of fully stateless probabilistic routing was rejected for high-customer-impact tenants.
rollout_plan:
1) Unit + integration tests in CI.
2) Feature flag gate: staged rollout to internal beta tenants.
3) Canary: 5% of production traffic (low-risk tenants) with verbose telemetry.
4) Monitor decision false positives and latency for 72 hours; roll forward to 25% then 100% if stable.
5) Enable for P1/P0 tenants after 2 successful waves.

Rollback criteria: >0.5% increase in 5m customer-visible errors or decision latency regression >10% p95.
comments: 2026-02-13 - Aisha Raman: Drafted initial design after on-call incident where a spike in 429s caused full-region failover for several mid-tier tenants. Uploaded design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Per-Request+Signal+Classifier

2026-02-20 - Marcus Green: Implemented prototype classifier in router-core branch feature/signal-classifier. Initial microbenchmarks show classifier cost ~0.9ms p95 without redis lookups. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router-core/pull/5893

2026-02-25 - UX/PM review (Daniel Cho): Need explicit telemetry fields for Console to show root cause; added requirement to acceptance criteria. Also called out tenant policy UI for follow-up (PM-448).

2026-03-02 - SRE (Priya Singh): Raised concern about redis hotkeys for tenants with bursty traffic; suggested sharded key naming and local bloom filter to avoid thundering herds. Added as technical note.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Green: Added probation logic and DECAYING state to the state machine. Updated redis TTL strategy: 30s probation TTL, exponential decay up to 1 hour. Ran synthetic surge test against staging: localized isolations observed, global variants unaffected. Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/goto/abcd1234

2026-03-08 - Security review (initial): Reviewed data stored in redis; no PII but tenant ids considered sensitive; will use hashed shard key and ensure encryption-in-transit. Security sign-off scheduled for 2026-03-12.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Green: Performance tuning: moved short-window aggregates to router's in-memory ring buffer to avoid a redis read on every request. Redis now consulted only on probation state transitions. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router-core/pull/5940
